raw.title: Senior Field Strategist, Cement
raw.excerpt: About UsHeavy industry is the foundation of modern society.
raw.description:
About Us

Heavy industry is the foundation of modern society. We need materials like cement, steel, and aluminum more than ever to rebuild our bridges and roads, construct wind and solar projects, and manufacture the electric vehicles and heat pumps that will undergird our future. But industry needs a second revolution. For as much as industry made the middle class and ushered in a remarkable era of prosperity for many, it also threatens our climate, reinforces environmental racism, wastes valuable materials and energy, and leaves communities and workers behind.

At Industrious Labs, our mission is to set into motion unstoppable policies, people power, and analysis to make a triple impact on climate, justice, and jobs — drastically reduce dangerous emissions, and make industry accountable to communities and working people. Over our first five years, we have grown from a $1M to a ~$10M annual operating budget, across a 501(c)(3) organization and an aligned LLC, with 26 U.S.-based staff and a growing international portfolio.

We are led by a team of four executives rather than a single executive director — a structure that reflects our commitment to distributed leadership and democratic decision-making. We are deliberately collaborative, equity-centered, and mission-driven. Everyone at Industrious Labs genuinely believes in this work, and that shared conviction is one of our greatest strengths.

About the Position

Industrious Labs is at an inflection point with our international cement work. Demand for cement sits squarely in the Global South, where nearly 90% of the world's new cement will be produced to build housing, roads, mass transit systems, and infrastructure to support economic growth and people's needs. The next several years are a decisive window to decarbonize this demand. People must have access to affordable, sustainable cement to meet housing and infrastructure development needs. It’s also vital that construction trades that use cement remain robust to support livelihoods and pathways to build wealth.

The Senior Field Strategist will sit within the Field Building team, reporting to Dominique Thomas and working in close collaboration with our Global cement team. Industrious Labs is fully remote, and we are open to US-based and International candidates. International candidates can not be more than 8 hours from the EST time zone.

The Senior Field Strategist is a highly skilled relationship builder with the expertise to effectively establish, grow, and sustain diverse coalitions of stakeholders. The Senior Field Strategist is energized by the challenge of the climate crisis, inspired to step into a new era of the movement, and has a strong track record of working with diverse groups such as organized labor, environmental justice advocates, and policymakers. This is a public-facing role for an equity-centered leader with a solid track record of working in coalition with others and building capacity and collective vision across diverse perspectives and experiences. In doing so, the Senior Field Strategist further establishes Industrious Labs as a national leader in industrial decarbonization and a go-to resource for policymakers, policy influencers, climate advocates, and community leaders.

The Senior Field Strategist holds key responsibilities that will evolve over time as the team grows and functions are distributed.

This role will work with colleagues on the cement team to meet the following key areas:

  • Major policy wins in priority nations/regions such as Africa, India, Southeast Asia, and Brazil by the end of 2030, with early evidence of impact.
  • International Finance Corporation (IFC) revises its performance standard incorporating our linguistic recommendations that are 1.5°C aligned and informed by our Global South partners.
  • The Network grows from existing champion organizations of low-carbon cement across countries with in-nation tables to 40+ organizations across 12-15 nations by the end of 2030.
  • Local partners in priority nations are actively engaged and committed to co-developing and implementing the campaign strategy, leading in-nation advocacy, and Network expansion.

The following responsibilities will be a part of the Senior Field Strategist's primary role.

  • Recruit and build an aligned and powerful Global Cement Network with a shared vision, theory of change, and capacity-building strategy for cement transformation. This includes increasing membership, holding consistent organizing 1:1s to build relationships, and ensuring a clear strategy to move to Global South ownership.
  • Execute a comprehensive field-building vision and strategy in key locations with partners that aligns with our field-building department and organizational mission and vision, which could include development of landscape assessments and/or power analyses.
  • Engage and build new relationships with key leaders, organizations, and partners in strategy development to build support for the cement campaign's goals that reflect our values and priorities around equity and justice.
  • Collaborate in the development of comprehensive advocacy plans that build a cohesive movement with the power necessary to win cement transformation in Sub-Saharan Africa, India, Southeast Asia, Brazil and beyond.
  • Develop a clear strategy to move regranting dollars to organizational partners in a justice-oriented manner. Be a thought partner to foundations and other regrantors in the space and ensure there is a coordinated, impactful strategy to maximize impact.
  • Design and implement trainings and other opportunities for stakeholders to collaborate, train each other, and build the foundational knowledge to develop and refine campaign approaches.
  • Identify partners with aligned efforts to accelerate action and leverage resources, relationships, and research.

The Successful Candidate

The incoming Senior Field Strategist is driven by their belief and commitment to Industrious Labs’ vision, mission, and values. Through their track record and expertise as an organizer and convener – optimally within the climate or another social justice movement – the successful candidate will play a vital role in the development and execution of the cement campaign. The Senior Field Strategist builds authentic and lasting relationships with communities and organizations impacted by pollution from industrial facilities, engaging them as partners in our mission. The successful candidate brings a mindset that considers capacity building the foundation of the vision we see for the future and sees transformational power building as necessary to win and dismantle systems of oppression.

The Senior Field Strategist joins a deeply committed team with a track record of success in campaign strategy, data analysis, and communications, focusing on climate and clean energy. The successful candidate is entrepreneurial and excited about the prospect of working collaboratively internally and building new partnerships within the climate movement. They have the experience of setting vision, establishing, and scaling successful programs with an ethos of creativity, humility, and an expectation of continual learning. They are excited and inspired by the challenge.

Despite enormous obstacles involved in decarbonizing heavy industry, the Industrious Labs team operates with a spirit of possibilities and seeks a Senior Field Strategist who shares the belief that we can all do things we’ve never done before and can stretch ourselves to achieve incredible results.

This role requires a deep commitment to the principles of justice and equity, proven collaboration skills, and the skill to design and execute coordinated strategies that will generate change in a deeply entrenched and seemingly intractable aspect of the climate movement. The Senior Field Strategist demonstrates leadership by diving right in to take a concept from idea to implementation, navigating through internal and external barriers as they arise without getting stuck, and finding and deploying resources creatively to solve problems. The selected candidate will also possess most of the following Core and ideally some of the Preferred qualifications:

Senior Field Strategist Core Qualifications

  • At least 5-8 years of increasing responsibility in robust coalition development, power building, and capacity/field/movement building, with a track record of accomplishment. Specifically:
    • Experience creating a clear vision with attainable goals that build power centered around equity and justice.
    • Experience developing and implementing a power analysis, community mapping, and/or landscape assessment. This includes the skill to articulate key findings and patterns.
    • Experience assisting/leading strategy development in coalition spaces and/or with diverse people/perspectives.
    • Experience designing/implementing organizing efforts in local, state, regional, national and/or international settings that build long-term sustainable power to win.
    • Strong analysis of movement theory, implementation, and the intersectionality of racial capitalism and other systems of oppression.
  • Effective relationship-building skills and solid existing relationships with a wide range of diverse external constituencies, from big greens, labor, environmental justice communities, etc.
  • Experience in the climate movement or another social justice movement.
  • Experience in community organizing or other forms of organizing
  • Ability and willingness to travel internationally on a semi-frequent basis

Senior Field Strategist Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working internationally and familiarity with the international advocacy and civil society landscape in the Global South.
  • Can be located in an international time zone that is not more than 8 hours from the Eastern Time Zone.
  • Entrepreneurial drive to build an organization from the ground up; prior start-up experience as an early team member in a growing organization
  • Experience re-granting with partners and moving resources equitably.
  • Experience in community organizing or other forms of organizing

Industrious Labs Core Qualifications

Below are the qualifications expected of all Industrious Labs staff.

  • Strong commitment to the mission, vision, policies, and goals of Industrious Labs.
  • Highly collaborative work style with the ability to operate as a peer and thought partner to colleagues and external partners.
  • Commitment to continuous learning, hunger for knowledge, and willingness to ask questions and self-correct; a curious, self-directed, and entrepreneurial approach.
  • Exceptional oral and written communication skills with the ability to break down a complex issue into manageable and clear decision points that drive the desired campaign outcomes.
  • Excited rather than intimidated by the challenge of what's unknown about this role.
  • Proven leadership skills with clarity of vision and a commitment to the highest levels of integrity, quality, and collaboration, developing strong team cultures, promoting and enhancing equity, diversity, and inclusion, performance management, and professional development.
  • Demonstrated experience working across lines of race, class, gender, and geography and an analysis of how climate change intersects with historically oppressed and marginalized communities.
  • Proven ability to prioritize and be flexible in a fast-paced, constantly evolving, and collaborative environment, where working on a team and working individually are all required.
  • Commitment to giving and receiving direct, compassionate feedback.

Salary and Benefits:

The annual salary for this position is $121,000. Industrious Labs has a policy not to negotiate salaries. Historically, negotiations reward those who have the skill, privilege, and confidence to ask for more money; and because not everyone has those skills, allowing for negotiations undermines the economic equity we strive for as an organization. Rather than use negotiations to drive competitive salaries, we endeavor to pay people well and establish a transparent salary scale based on the experience, competencies, and responsibilities required to thrive in this role.

Industrious Labs offers a competitive set of benefits, including comprehensive health care coverage, a work-from-home stipend, retirement plan options, paid holidays plus unlimited vacation, starting with a minimum of 15 business days.

Our Commitment to Racial Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Climate Justice:

We believe that diversity in our team isn’t just a value but brings different experiences and perspectives essential to solving the climate crisis. If you’ve read this job description and are excited by it and can see yourself happily filling this role and making a difference on climate change, we hope you apply. Industrious Labs recognizes that a variety of different educational or professional pathways could lead to being a strong candidate and contributor for this role. You may have transferable skills from experiences that may not match exactly what we’ve called out in our list of qualifications for this position. We’d love to hear about your experience and the skills you would bring to serve in this role. Industrious Labs is an equal-opportunity employer and is committed to transparent and equitable recruitment, hiring, and promotion processes that foster inclusion and belonging. If you need reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please email Heather Beckford at .

A Note About Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Please provide your original thoughts and ideas in your cover letter and answers to our questions. We hope to understand how you think your experience may contribute to being successful at Industrious Labs! Your authentic and unique perspective is important to us. We value this opportunity to gain an understanding of your independent thoughts without the use of artificial input or search tools.

We understand that your resume may have been built or developed with AI; however, your resume should represent your qualifications and skills accurately. Otherwise, the use of AI in our hiring process, including responses to interview questions, thought exercises or writing prompts, may disqualify your candidacy.

Application Procedure:

To apply, please submit a resume and original cover letter answering the following:

  1. What motivates you to spend your time, skills, and expertise working on climate change?
  2. How do you describe power? How have you built power with others in the past?
  3. Do you have experience working with diverse populations internationally? If so, please describe that experience. If you do not have that experience, please describe what skills you believe you would need to build and what support you would need to do global/international work?

This position is open until filled. Candidate review and phone screens begin immediately and will continue throughout the search. We anticipate several steps of mutual exploration, including a phone screen, panel interview(s), and thought exercises for finalist candidates. Our search processes generally take 3 - 4 months.

Shape the future of defense with MANTECH! Join a team dedicated to safeguarding our nation through advanced tech and innovative solutions. MANTECH seeks a career and customer-oriented Senior Tactical Aviation Operations Lead in Lexington Park, MD.This position offers remote work, but the individual must be available for CONUS travel as needed.

This role will provide operational subject matter expertise for a critical Department of Defense Modeling & Simulation (M&S) initiative. This role is integral to bridging operational reality with advanced software systems, guiding development efforts that ensure tactical relevance and mission effectiveness. You will advise government stakeholders as a Trusted Operational Advisor, leveraging extensive military experience to shape digital simulation environments that accurately reflect modern combat scenarios.

Responsibilities may include but are not limited to:

  • Evaluating Government Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) and Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solutions to recommend tools that balance delivery schedules, fidelity, and mission alignment

  • Leading requirements development and refinement to ensure simulation systems support validated operational use cases and mission-critical outcomes

  • Championing the integration of Agile development practices and digital engineering workflows within operational testing and evaluation processes

  • Designing and overseeing the creation of realistic, high-fidelity tactical scenarios for use in synthetic training and evaluation environments

  • Leading test and evaluation (T&E) activities, including flight and ground event support, with expert interpretation of simulation and stimulation system performance

  • Directing the development and delivery of user-focused training materials to ensure effective employment of simulation capabilities by operational personnel

  • Leading operational SME teams to resolve complex issues, ensure alignment with operational goals, and manage task execution across the contract lifecycle. Leading engagements with key program stakeholders.

  • Must be available for CONUS travel as needed

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution

  • 12+ years of experience supporting military tactical operations and tactical aviation system development

  • Prior military service as a commissioned officer with demonstrated expertise in operational employment of tactical aviation platforms

  • Previously qualified strike lead

  • Experience with 5th Generation fighter tactical employment

  • Developmental or Operational Test experience in a tactical aviation platform

  • Demonstrated success leading cross-functional teams and solving mission-critical problems in operational or technical environments

  • Demonstrated ability to present complex tactical trade-offs and solution recommendations to senior government stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience supporting system development and testing of defense technologies

  • Experience supporting Joint Simulation Environment (JSE) or distributed battlespace modeling initiatives (NCTE, DMON)

  • Familiarity with incorporating operational SME feedback into Agile software development sprints and DevSecOps pipelines

  • Weapons School or Test Pilot School Graduate

Clearance Requirements:

  • Must possess an active Top Secret clearance with current SCI eligibility

Physical Requirements:

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position approximately 50% of the time

  • Occasionally required to move throughout office spaces to access equipment, files, or interact with co-workers

  • Must be able to enter and exit simulator cockpits and fly simulated missions

  • Must be able to effectively communicate with team members, leadership, and customers, including in presentation settings, and convey accurate technical information


The projected compensation range for this position is $165,900.00-$295,300.00. There are differentiating factors that can impact a final salary/hourly rate, including, but not limited to, Contract Wage Determination, relevant work experience, skills and competencies that align to the specified role, geographic location (For Remote Opportunities), education and certifications as well as Federal Government Contract Labor categories. MANTECH’s benefits offerings include, dependent upon position, Health Insurance, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, Holiday Pay, short-term and long-term Disability, Retirement and Savings, Learning and Development opportunities, wellness programs as well as other optional benefit elections.

MANTECH considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to disability or veteran status or any other status protected under any federal, state, or local law or regulation.

Preferred Qualifications:

Senior OCM Consultant

As a Senior OCM Consultant, you will help organizations successfully navigate complex technology implementations and business transformation initiatives by focusing on the people side of change. In partnership with OCM leaders, client stakeholders, and cross-functional project teams, you will design and deliver change strategies that build readiness, strengthen engagement, accelerate adoption, and support lasting business outcomes.

This role is ideal for a consultant who brings both strategic perspective and hands-on execution—someone who can translate complexity into clear action, influence stakeholders at all levels, and deliver practical solutions that help leaders and employees embrace new systems, processes, and ways of working.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate technical and process changes into clear business impacts and user-focused messaging.
  • Strong consulting, facilitation, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience working in matrixed project environments and collaborating with cross-functional business and technical teams.
  • Excellent organizational skills with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
  • Comfortable working in fast-paced environments with evolving priorities and ambiguity.
  • Bachelor’s degree required; degree in Business, Communications, Organizational Development, or a related field preferred.

Experienced Clinical Project Manager – Cell & Gene Therapy (Sponsor Dedicated/ Remote: US only)

Syneos Health® is a leading fully integrated biopharmaceutical solutions organization built to accelerate customer success. We translate unique clinical, medical affairs and commercial insights into outcomes to address modern market realities.

Our Clinical Development model brings the customer and the patient to the center of everything that we do. We are continuously looking for ways to simplify and streamline our work to not only make Syneos Health easier to work with, but to make us easier to work for.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to accelerate the delivery of therapies, because we are passionate to change lives.

Discover what our 29,000 employees, across 110 countries already know:

WORK HERE MATTERS EVERYWHERE

Why Syneos Health

  • We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
  • We are committed to our Total Self culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Our Total Self culture is what unites us globally, and we are dedicated to taking care of our people.
  • We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because when we bring together diversity of thoughts, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives – we’re able to create a place where everyone feels like they belong.

Job Responsibilities

Clinical Project Manager I – Sponsor Dedicated (Cell & Gene Therapy)

Remote- US Based only

Role Summary

We are seeking a skilled and motivated Project Manager I to join our sponsor-dedicated team supporting high-impact oncology and cell & gene therapy trials, including CAR-T studies. In this role, you will work full-time on behalf of a leading biopharmaceutical sponsor while employed within a global CRO—offering the best of both worlds: sponsor collaboration and CRO resources.

This position focuses on early-phase trial execution, operational oversight, and cross-functional coordination across global study teams.

What You Will Do

  • Act as a sponsor-facing project manager, ensuring the successful execution of assigned CAR-T and gene therapy trials from startup through closeout.

  • Lead or support study start-up, site activation, and enrollment, working closely with site monitors, regulatory teams, and contracts personnel.

  • Serve as a key point of contact across internal (CRO) and sponsor teams, facilitating regular communications, status reporting, and governance updates.

  • Coordinate with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure timelines, budgets, and milestones are met, particularly in complex, high-touch studies.

  • Track and manage protocol compliance, CAPAs, and site-level quality indicators; support resolution of audit findings.

  • Ensure inspection readiness and regulatory compliance by overseeing TMF maintenance, data accuracy, and documentation completeness.

  • Manage or contribute to the tracking of low-stability endpoint samples and IP-related processes, ensuring timely lab delivery and site support.

  • Assist with risk identification and mitigation planning, while continuously optimizing trial execution processes.

Skills and Experience You Have

  • 2–4 years of clinical trial experience, preferably in a CRO setting, with a focus on oncology, rare disease, or gene-modified cell therapy trials.

  • Prior involvement in CAR-T or other cell therapy studies is highly desirable.

  • Strong familiarity with GCP/ICH guidelines, FDA/EMA regulations, and inspection-readiness standards.

  • Experience working in sponsor-dedicated or embedded roles within a CRO is a plus.

  • Proficiency in clinical systems (e.g., CTMS, EDC, eTMF) and project management tools.

  • Confident in leading sponsor calls, presenting KPIs, and contributing to operational governance.

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (Life Sciences, Nursing, Pharmacy, etc.) or equivalent work experience.

  • Comfortable with remote work but agreeable to occasional in-person collaboration in Los Angeles.

Why You Want to Work Here

  • Work sponsor-side, stay CRO-strong: This sponsor-dedicated role offers the visibility and strategic engagement of working directly with a biotech leader, while maintaining CRO support and infrastructure.

  • Advance life-saving research: Be a part of cutting-edge cell and gene therapy trials, helping bring breakthrough therapies to patients faster.

  • Grow your career intentionally: Gain exposure to high-impact projects with opportunities to step up into larger roles and leadership paths.

  • Collaborate where it counts: Enjoy the flexibility of remote work with access to in-office opportunities that foster deeper team integration and mentorship.

  • Be mission-aligned: Work with a team that shares your urgency, attention to detail, and dedication to patients battling cancer and rare diseases.

Why Join Us?

This role offers the opportunity to do more than manage clinical trials — it’s a chance to be at the center of some of the most promising therapeutic advancements in the world. You’ll play a critical role in accelerating the development of treatments that could change patients’ lives forever.

If you're looking to grow your career while making a real-world impact, we invite you to apply and join a mission that matters.

We are always excited to connect with great talent. This posting is intended for a [possible] upcoming opportunity rather than a live role. By expressing your interest, you'll be added to our talent pipeline and considered should this role become available.

At  Syneos Health, we believe in providing an environment and culture in which Our People can thrive, develop and advance. We reward and recognize our people by providing valuable benefits and a quality-of-life balance. The benefits for this position may include a company car or car allowance, Health benefits to include Medical, Dental and Vision, Company match 401k, eligibility to participate in Employee Stock Purchase Plan, Eligibility to earn commissions/bonus based on company and individual performance, and flexible paid time off (PTO) and sick time. Because certain states and municipalities have regulated paid sick time requirements, eligibility for paid sick time may vary depending on where you work. Syneos complies with all applicable federal, state, and municipal paid sick time requirements.

Salary Range:

The base salary range represents the anticipated low and high of the Syneos Health range for this position. Actual salary will vary based on various factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role.

Get to know Syneos Health

Over the past 5 years, we have worked with 94% of all Novel FDA Approved Drugs, 95% of EMA Authorized Products and over 200 Studies across 73,000 Sites and 675,000+ Trial patients.

No matter what your role is, you’ll take the initiative and challenge the status quo with us in a highly competitive and ever-changing environment. Learn more about Syneos Health.

Role Overview

In this role, you'll combine leadership, operational excellence, and industry expertise to support agents, customers, and business partners while ensuring compliance and underwriting quality standards. As a trusted subject matter expert, you'll tackle complex underwriting challenges, support key business decisions, and champion best practices throughout the region. If you're a relationship-focused leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is passionate about helping agriculture succeed, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

In this Exciting Opportunity, You Will:

  • Oversee underwriting operations, maintain workflow expertise, assist with business processing as needed, and support departmental staffing during absences or peak workloads.

  • Evaluate underwriting information, make final underwriting determinations, and prepare and process policies and endorsements.

  • Support business unit initiatives by gathering and evaluating information, planning and implementing processes and systems, and promoting strategic projects, including ProAgWorks implementation and training.

  • Develop, maintain, and interpret underwriting guidelines, FCIC documentation, and Underwriting Manual (TOPE) standards to ensure consistency and compliance.

  • Analyze policy data, support FCIC error resolution efforts, monitor underwriting quality metrics, and manage reporting activities.

  • Serve as a subject matter expert by responding to complex inquiries and providing underwriting support to agents, policyholders, applicants, account representatives, clients, and underwriters.

What You Bring

  • A minimum of six years of relevant and progressive professional experience within underwriting.

  • Previous agriculture or crop insurance industry experience.

  • A bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Business Administration, or a related field, or the equivalent education and/or experience.

  • Possess the ability to apply knowledge of principles, practices, and procedures of underwriting in day-to-day and strategic work.

  • Solid written and verbal communication skills with an emphasis on confidentiality, tact, and diplomacy to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.

  • Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.

  • Knowledgeable of industry changes, legal updates, and technical developments related to applicable area of the Company's business to proactively respond to changing business environment.

What We Offer

  • Strong learning culture with ongoing development opportunities

  • Opportunities for growth and career advancement

  • Comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, with eligibility beginning on your first day of employment

  • Basic life and disability insurance

  • 401(k) plan with 6% company match

  • 20 days of PTO, three floating holidays, approximately 10 paid holidays, and volunteer time off

  • Paid parental leave

  • Access to our award-winning wellness program, including mental health services, fitness network membership, and a complimentary Headspace subscription

  • Student loan matching program

  • Employee discount program

  • An opportunity to do meaningful work and love what you do

What We Represent:

A career with purpose. Our crop insurance professionals work each day to bring peace of mind and protection to American farmers and ranchers. Join a team who truly cares.

  • Part of something bigger: We offer a career with purpose as you support the farmers and ranchers who create food, fuel, and fiber for the world.

  • Personal connections: We are built on strong relationships and appreciation of your individuality.

  • A team who cares: We look out for each other personally and professionally because we care about each other.

  • Innovators by trade: We’re committed to a brighter tomorrow for our team members and agriculture.

The Company:

ProAg, a member of the Tokio Marine HCC group of companies, is positioned as a financially strong and well-capitalized insurer with an AM Best rating of A++. With 100 years of service to our agents & insureds, we stand committed to continuing the principles that ProAg was founded on: Integrity, Loyalty, and Customer Service.

Tokio Marine HCC is a leading specialty insurance group with offices in the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe, and other exciting locations. With the strength and stability that comes from being a member of the Tokio Marine Group, and more than fifty years of growth, profitability, and stability, we offer important insurance products that most people don’t even know exist. Every policy we write is special, enabling our clients to do amazing things.

Where the hiring and employment of individuals is not restricted by the foregoing, the Company will consider qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history in compliance with applicable law such as the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the San Diego Fair Chance Ordinance, and the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.]

Job Summary:

Plans, coordinates, and oversees procedures and processes of the Provider Credentialing Program in compliance with regulatory requirements. Ensures compliance with all credentialing and privileging requirements of applicable regulatory agencies. Conducts background investigations on physicians and other providers applying for affiliation including licensure, education and post-graduate clinical training, board certification, disciplinary actions and other professional sanctions, malpractice history, and peer assessment of current competence at time of appointment, reappointment, and cross credentialing.

Job Duties:

Preferred experience in Echo or Credential Stream

  • Reviews and analyzes physician applications and credentialing documents including certificates of education, residency and fellowship training, board certification and eligibility, licensure, professional work history, liability insurance and malpractice history.
  • Assesses completeness of information and providers' qualifications relative to established standards.
  • Reviews and analyzes primary source verification for licensure, certification or registration required to practice a profession.
  • Requests, maintains, and ensures competency data is present at appointment and re-appointment.
  • Maintains tracking of all new providers drug screening, background checks, child abuse clearance, finger printing, code of conduct, disruptive practitioner policies, current clinical competency data and Health Service information for new providers.
  • Maintains a working knowledge of applicable regulatory agencies.
  • Immediately reports to manager any collected information which may be averse to an applicant.
  • Identifies and flags adverse information from application materials for the purpose of conducting special follow-up investigations in preparation for credentialing review.
  • Maintains an understanding of the third-party payor requirements.
  • Prepares and screens, mails letter, tracks and responds daily.
  • Employs public relations skills in a wide variety of phone contacts with external sources for purposes of soliciting information essential to credentials investigations, including licensing agencies; university and hospital training program administrators; certification boards; liability insurance carriers; hospital officials and credentials staff; and physicians and their office staffs.
  • Organizes and maintains physician files and information following confidentiality guidelines, performs varied clerical support functions.
  • Internally audits and maintains physician files in accordance with established principles of legal documentation and confidentiality.
  • Prepare all files monthly for Credentials Committee review and follow-up on Credentials Committee Decisions.
  • Establish and maintain excellent relationship and good communication channels with physicians, office staff, and practice administrators.
  • Assist with Special projects (i.e., physician education, JCAHO and Department of Health Preparation, clinical competency data, life supports)
  • Maintain a thorough understanding of the standards of JCAHO, Department of Health, Bylaws, Rules and Regulation of the Medical Staff, and other regulatory agencies as appropriate.
  • Maintains provider database and manipulates database to extract information for ad hoc reports, surveys, and internal and external provider directory extracts.
  • Adapts software as needed to facilitate efficient operation of credentials department and continuous quality improvement.

Work is typically performed in an office environment. Accountable for satisfying all job specific obligations and complying with all organization policies and procedures. The specific statements in this profile are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements considered necessary to successfully perform the job.

This posting reflects an opening for Credentialing Coordinator II and we are seeking candidates for that position. Geisinger reserves the right to consider applicants for higher level of this role based on their skills, qualifications, and experience. We encourage all qualified individuals to apply.

  • EXCELLENCE: We treasure colleagues who humbly strive for excellence.

Job Title: Workflow Manager, Pharmacovigilance Operations (Specialist II, PSS) Remote

Job Location: Durham

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Workflow Manager, Pharmacovigilance Operations (Specialist II, PSS) US or Canada Remote

Fortrea is seeking a Workflow Manager, Pharmacovigilance Operations (Specialist II, PSS) is responsible for supporting and overseeing Clinical Safety and Pharmacovigilance Services (PSS) operations associated with safety data collected from clinical trials and post-marketing programs. The role is accountable for managing end-to-end safety case workflows, ensuring adverse events are processed, tracked, and progressed through all workflow stages in accordance with client requirements, regulatory obligations, and agreed timelines.

The position is responsible for coordinating workflow activities across safety operations, monitoring case progression and compliance metrics, identifying and resolving workflow delays, and ensuring efficient utilization of resources to support high-quality service delivery. The Workflow Manager provides operational support to client project teams and standalone programs while maintaining compliance with applicable pharmacovigilance regulations, company procedures, and quality standards.

The incumbent is expected to comply with the legal requirements of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, the COSHH Regulations 1989, and the EC (European Commission) Directives 1992/3, as documented in the Company's Health and Safety Manual.

Summary of Responsibilities:

  • Manage the receipt and processing of all adverse event reports reported either spontaneously from any source or solicited from a clinical trial including safety database entry, AE review, write patient narratives with coding, follow-up of missing information, lists assessment against appropriate label (For Marketed products, if applicable).
  • Submission of expedited Serious Adverse Event (SAE) reports to clients, Regulatory Authorities, Ethics Committees, investigators, third party vendors, Partners and Fortrea project personnel, if required & as agreed with client during study set-up, within study specified timelines.
  • Ensure all cases that require expediting reporting to worldwide Regulatory Agencies or other recipients are prioritized for processing and submission within the regulatory and/or study specific applicable timelines.
  • Work with Data Management or client on reconciliation of safety databases, if appropriate.
  • Support audit or inspection preparations.
  • Any other duties as assigned by management.

Qualifications (Minimum Required):

  • Non-degree + 2-3 years of Safety experience or 5 years of relevant experience
  • Associate degree + 2-3 years of Safety experience or 4 years of relevant experience
  • BS/BA + 2 years of safety experience or 3-4 years of relevant experience
  • MS/MA + 2 years of safety experience or 2-3 years of relevant experience
  • PharmD + 2 years of safety experience or 2-3 years relevant experience

For PharmD, a one-year residency of fellowship can be considered as relevant experience

* Safety experience includes actual experience processing AE/SAE reports, generating narratives, queries, working within safety databases, and experience with regulatory submissions.

Experience (Minimum Required):

  • Minimum of 2 years of pharmacovigilance (PV) work experience. Experience supporting U.S. and/or Canadian regulatory environments is preferred.
  • Advanced command of English language, including speaking, writing, and reading.
  • Strong knowledge of safety databases (e.g., Argus), workflow tracking systems, and case management tools
  • Strong organizational and project management skills
  • Analytical mindset with problem-solving capabilities
  • Good understanding of ICH guidelines and global regulatory requirements for the reporting of adverse events for both marketed and investigational products.

Preferred Experience:

  • 4-5 years of experience in pharmacovigilance or drug safety operations
  • Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and relevant experience will also be
    considered.
Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the country in which they reside (United States or Canada). Fortrea is unable to provide current or future employment sponsorship for this position.

***This is a INDIVIDUAL CONTRIBUTOR role.***

Work Environment:

  • Work is performed in a remote based office environment with exposure to electrical office equipment.
  • Occasional drives to site locations with occasional travel both domestic and international.

Physical Requirements:

  • Frequently stationary for 6-8 hours per day.

Summary

We are a healthcare technology company at the forefront of clinical AI innovation, dedicated to transforming real-world clinical practice through intelligent, user-centered design. As a mid-level UX/UI Designer, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the user experience of clinician- and patient-facing interfaces across our product suite, including Clinical Interact. You will translate strategic design direction into clear, accessible, and implementation-ready interfaces, ensuring that complex clinical data is presented with clarity and precision under time-sensitive conditions. Working closely with cross-functional teams—including engineering, AI, and clinical experts—you will help build intuitive, personalized, and scalable experiences that empower healthcare providers and improve patient outcomes. This role is ideal for a designer who thrives in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment and is passionate about blending technical rigor with deep clinical empathy.

Responsibilities

  • Design intuitive, high-fidelity interfaces for clinician- and patient-facing screens that present dense clinical data—such as ranked findings, knowledge-graph-driven insights, and confidence indicators—clearly and effectively under time pressure.

  • Extend and maintain the design system by leveraging and contributing to color tokens, typography, component libraries, and design tokens—avoiding ad hoc styles.
  • Design for dynamic personalization models, including variable content density, tile states, and adaptive content prioritization, to ensure usability across diverse clinical and patient contexts.
  • Deliver clean, developer-ready handoffs in Figma, including detailed specs, redlines, component states, and interactive prototypes for front-end engineering teams.
  • Partner with clinical and AI teams to integrate usability feedback, clinical insights, and real-world testing findings into iterative design improvements.

Requirements

Requirements:
  • 3–5 years of professional UX/UI design experience, with a portfolio showcasing shipped products and real-world impact.
  • Expert proficiency in Figma, including auto-layout, component variants, design systems, and dev-mode handoff workflows.
  • Proven experience designing data-dense interfaces in complex domains such as clinical software, dashboards, financial systems, or similar high-information environments.
  • Solid understanding of accessibility standards, including WCAG AA compliance, with practical application in design decisions.
  • Preference for candidates based in the Middle East or between the timezone of GMT+3 - GMT+8.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience designing for healthcare, clinical workflows, or medical software environments.
  • Familiarity with design tokens, design-system architecture, and scalable component design.
  • Demonstrated ability to design adaptive, context-aware, or personalized interfaces beyond static screen designs.

Core Competencies

  • Exceptional ability to establish clear information hierarchy in complex, high-pressure scenarios.
  • Strong collaborative mindset with the ability to work effectively across engineering, AI, and clinical teams.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and adapting quickly within a fast-moving startup environment.
  • Deep clinical empathy and a user-first mindset focused on the real-world needs of clinicians and patients.

Cofactr is on a mission to empower those who get the critical work done. We're bridging the gaps left by traditional supply chain management solutions, creating a seamless link between Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) through our innovative BOM to Build Platform, specifically tailored for Hardware innovators. Our platform revolutionizes the technical hardware supply chain by ensuring it is precise, efficient, and effortlessly manageable. As a proud member of the Y Combinator W22 cohort, we've seen our revenue grow consistently, supported by substantial venture funding from esteemed VCs, including Bain Capital Ventures.

The Team

At Cofactr, we're committed to fostering efficiency, scalability, and innovation. We are transforming the landscape of hardware manufacturing with our comprehensive ecosystem of Supply chain tools, designed to streamline processes and enable new possibilities.

The Role

Our procurement team works in conjunction with our managed services team to process and track customer orders. As the Procurement Associate, you will use the Cofactr platform to place orders through API ordering and manually via supplier websites. In addition, you will be responsible for tracking order progress and updating the Cofactr platform accordingly to provide full visibility for our customers and their order status. Due to the varying nature of the electronics industry, you will keep track of changing lead times, delayed parts, and possible supplier decommits.

What You'll Do

  • Process purchase lines using the distributor API ordering and manually placing orders through websites.
  • Learn and use the Cofactr platform to confirm, track, and adjust orders as needed.
  • Ensure that all of the data shown to our customers is accurate regarding lead times and arrival estimates to the best of our ability.
  • Problem-solving procurement issues related to delayed parts, decommits, and other availability issues. If necessary, remediate purchase lines.
  • Quote complete BOMs for customers using our price-solving software.
  • Contact suppliers for individual part quotes, lead times, and other info.
  • Report software bugs and issues to our front-end engineering team.
  • Report data discrepancies and issues to our data team.

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years working in procurement in the field of electronics for a contractor manufacturer/EMS or electronics OEM is required
  • Knowledge of basic electronics supply chain terms and issues - MOQ, manufacturer leads times, part decommits, end-user restrictions, and statements
  • Experience working with PCBA and procurement BOMs
  • Comfortable learning new software quickly
  • Able to keep track of and organize significant amounts of data.
  • Basic understanding of Excel and Google Suite
  • A good communicator who can effectively report issues and problems as they pop up.
  • Must be *very* detail-oriented.

Benefits

-Competitive salary and equity
-100% employee premium coverage of health, dental, and vision plans
-FSA offerings
-401(k) with 4% company matching
- Accrued Time off policy
- Commuter benefits with a company contribution

Kickstarter is the leading crowdfunding platform for creative projects across film, games, music, art, design, and technology. Since our founding in 2009, our mission to help bring creative projects to life has been powered by the people behind the work.

Together, we’ve helped creators around the world launch creative projects that have generated billions of dollars in pledges. That same commitment extends inward. Rooted in shared values, Kickstarter invests in the growth and success of our team, treating employees as whole people and empowering them with the autonomy and space to participate in decisions that shape their work and our company.

Kickstarter is seeking an Event Marketer to join our Marketing team, reporting to the Director, Brand and Communications. The right person can transform ambitious ideas into memorable, well-executed experiences for creators, backers, partners, and cultural communities.

This role combines creative thinking with exceptional experiential operational discipline. The Event Marketer will help shape the experience, identify what will make it distinctive, and manage the many details required to bring it to life—on time, within budget, and at a consistently high standard.

The right person is highly collaborative, deeply organized, resourceful with budgets, and connected to a strong network of vendors and production partners. They understand that great events are not simply gatherings; they are strategic expressions of the Kickstarter brand and opportunities to deepen relationships, create cultural relevance, and drive measurable outcomes.

The salary for this role in the United States is $120,000.

In this role, you will:

  • Plan and execute Kickstarter’s portfolio of brand, creator, category, industry, and community events.
  • Translate strategic and creative concepts into clear event plans, production timelines, budgets, and onsite experiences.
  • Collaborate with Brand, Communications, Outreach, Growth, Editorial & Content, and other teams to define each event’s audience, purpose, creative direction, and measures of success.
  • Develop event formats and experiences that feel distinctive to Kickstarter and meaningful to the communities we serve.
  • Own end-to-end event operations, including venues, vendors, production, staffing, travel, run-of-show, guest experience, risk planning, and onsite execution.
  • Source, negotiate with, and manage agencies, fabricators, production teams, venues, caterers, and other event partners.
  • Build and maintain a strong, diverse network of trusted vendors and cultural partners across key markets.
  • Manage event budgets with discipline and creativity, finding ways to maximize impact without compromising the quality of the experience.
  • Establish repeatable planning tools, processes, and standards that enable the team to execute efficiently across multiple events.
  • Anticipate challenges, make thoughtful decisions under pressure, and keep collaborators aligned throughout the planning process.
  • Partner with Communications and across Marketing to extend the impact of events through content, media, social amplification, and post-event engagement.
  • Evaluate event performance and apply insights to improve future programming and investment decisions.

About You

  • Experience producing brand, cultural, community, industry, or experiential events from concept through completion.
  • A strong creative instinct and the practical ability to turn an idea into a compelling physical or virtual experience.
  • Exceptional project management, organizational, and budget-management skills.
  • Established relationships with high-quality vendors, venues, production partners, and event specialists.
  • Confidence managing multiple workstreams, stakeholders, and deadlines without losing sight of the guest experience or strategic objective.
  • Strong negotiation skills and a reputation for being resourceful and responsible with budgets.
  • A calm, solutions-oriented approach to the inevitable changes and challenges of live and virtual events.
  • Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • An understanding of how events can support brand building, community development, relationship management, and business growth.
  • Enthusiasm for Kickstarter’s mission and the creative communities we serve.

What You'll Enjoy

  • A fully remote workforce with plenty of opportunities to get to know your colleagues
  • 100% employer-paid health plan offerings
  • 16 paid vacation days, 10 sick days, paid holidays, and a company-wide winter break between Christmas and New Years
  • 25 volunteer hours each year to give back to your community
  • 18 weeks of parental leave for the primary caregiver; 16 weeks of parental leave for the secondary caregiver, plus fertility/family planning resources
  • 401k with 3% safe harbor contribution
  • Annual stipends including a Remote Working & Wellness Stipend of $3,000 USD (prorated) each calendar year for expenses related to remote working, wellness, health, and fitness and a $500 Role Development Stipend
  • Kickstarter currently operates with a 4-day workweek, a model that aligns with our belief in a healthy work-life balance and gives staff the space to be more than their work
  • Incredibly talented and inspiring colleagues who know how to blend their creative endeavors into their work

You can read more about our benefits and working at Kickstarter at our Jobs page:

Our Fully Virtual Team

We’re currently able to support employees based in the following US locations: CA, CO, CT, GA, IL, MA, MD, NC, NJ, NY, OR, SC, VA, VT, and WA. We're also able to support employees in the United Kingdom. If you live in—or are willing to move to—any of these locations, we look forward to your application! If there is a required or preferred location for an open role, it will be listed in the job description.

  • Coordinate site selection work, including in market site visits when required, and preparation of site approval reviews supported by analysis and market conditions.

Franchise finance and transactions

  • Lead the international development finance scope, assessing franchisee financial health, capital structures, and growth readiness.
  • Partner with new franchisees to build business plans and capital and financial models, and to align development pace to returns and funding realities.
  • Lead transactional work tied to development outcomes, including acquisitions, divestitures, investments, and workouts, coordinating with internal partners as required.

Fees and cross functional coordination

  • Assist with collection of area and store fees across international markets, working with internal partners as appropriate.
  • Coordinate effectively with internal departments to deliver outcomes on time, including Concept Development, Marketing, Supply Chain, R and D, and Legal.

DECISION RIGHTS AND ACCOUNTABILITY

  • Accountable for building the market and partner pipeline, and for bringing partner recommendations and supporting diligence to the Executive Review Committee.
  • Accountable for negotiation of development agreement terms, and for ensuring internal legal and compliance processes are followed before execution.
  • Accountable for running the development approval process (site approvals, closures, renewals, franchisee approvals) and for escalating decisions that require committee or executive approval per company process.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

  • Higher quality partner pipeline, with partners that have the operational depth and financial capacity to develop and sustain growth.
  • Signed development agreements that match market potential and partner capability, with clear obligations and enforceable follow-through.
  • First sites in new markets opened with disciplined planning and cross functional coordination, without avoidable surprises in real estate, build, or compliance.
  • Franchisee capital plans and growth readiness assessed early, and development plans adjusted before problems show up in execution.
  • Existing development obligations tracked and enforced, with early intervention when performance drifts.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Special projects as assigned.

Education/Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree required or equivalent education and experience in lieu of degree. Master’s preferred in Business, Finance, or Commerce.

  • Domestic franchising experience is helpful.

Skills:

  • Strong analytical capability, including ability to build and review business plans and financial models tied to returns and capital plans.
  • Strong sales, negotiation, and deal making skills, with an established international network in franchising.
  • Cross cultural fluency and international savvy. Second or third language capability preferred
  • Strong organization, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple parallel workstreams under deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently and drive outcomes without heavy oversight.
  • Ability to collaborate across a matrixed organization and coordinate cross functional work to completion.

Other Requirements:

  • Frequent travel, up to 70%, sometimes short notice.

  • Ability to work evenings and occasional weekends to meet deadlines and communicate with international stakeholders across time zones.
  • Frequent communication via telephone and email, including outside standard hours due to international time zones.

Our benefit package supports the well-being of our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefit package includes, medical, dental, 401K match, paid time off (including volunteer time as well as parental leave) and so much more! Inclusion & Belonging

We are committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging for all who touch DQ. We believe in and commit to fostering a community where employees bring their authentic selves to work, and where we recruit, engage, and retain employees, franchise owners, and suppliers based on qualifications and merit. IDQ is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we use E-Verify to confirm the identity and employment eligibility of all new team members. You must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship.

Our Client

Our client is a Singapore-based multinational food and beverage company specializing in the production and distribution of instant beverages, particularly coffee mixes and non-dairy creamers. With a strong presence across Asia, Eastern Europe, and other emerging markets, the company focuses on delivering affordable, mass-market products while continuously optimizing cost efficiency and product formulations. Its operations are supported by manufacturing facilities, including in Malaysia, and it actively competes with Chinese producers by exploring innovations in ingredients and production processes to maintain competitiveness in pricing and quality.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct a comprehensive analysis of existing non-dairy creamer product formulations, focusing on cost structure, ingredient composition, and performance.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize formulation and reduce production costs while maintaining or improving product quality.
  • Provide insights into China-based manufacturing practices, including cost advantages, sourcing strategies, and formulation techniques.
  • Recommend alternative ingredients, suppliers, or processes to improve cost competitiveness against Chinese producers.
  • Work closely with internal teams (R&D, production, and business) to implement improvements and validate results.
  • Deliver clear, actionable reports and recommendations to senior stakeholders, including business leadership.
  • Support ongoing product development or reformulation initiatives as needed during the engagement period.
  • Participate in periodic on-site visits to the Malaysia facility to collaborate with local teams.

Location & Travel

  • Candidate can be based anywhere in China (to work remotely), with periodical travel to Malaysia (expenses covered).

Requirements

  • Minimum 10+ years of experience in food R&D or product development, specifically in non-dairy creamer or related powdered beverage products.
  • Proven experience working within manufacturing environments in China, with strong understanding of local cost structures and competitive practices.
  • Deep technical knowledge of formulation, ingredients, and processing for non-dairy creamer products.
  • Demonstrated track record of cost optimization or formulation improvement projects.
  • Ability to work in a consultative, advisory capacity and translate technical insights into business impact.
  • Comfortable working on a contract/freelance basis with flexible engagement structure (e.g., monthly advisory or project-based).
  • Willingness to travel to Malaysia periodically (expenses covered).
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently.
  • English proficiency preferred but not a must.

raw.description:
Overview

We need an ambitious, curious leader to become a Project Analyst on the Technology Team to help drive the biggest change in the company’s history.

The Opportunity – Why Join

Are you ready to redefine how an entire industry engages with customers? At AAA Life we leverage technology to put human connection at the heart of what we do. If you are someone who thrives on purpose and wants to make a tangible difference in people’s lives when it matters most, then join AAA Life who has the unique ability to access tens of millions of existing AAA customers powered by the strength of one of America’s most trusted brands. We have embarked on a mission to double in size - Becoming one of the largest providers in the US. These facts showcase why we're the right choice:

  • On purpose: a leading professional services firm found that the commitment, empathy and dedication of employees at AAA Life was the highest across a benchmark of top US companies
  • On growth: we have the privilege to offer our products to tens of millions of Americans that are proud members of AAA
  • On making a difference: we serve Americans by delivering life insurance products that make a true difference for families during their hardest times, not wealth management instruments (more details on this during the interview)
  • On culture: USA Today named us 2025 top workplace nationwide. We believe the job of an insurance company is to do good. Our mission is to help our members during what is often the hardest times in their lives. We pick up the phone to people who have lost loved ones and offer our genuine support. That is why we will always put human connection at the heart of what we do - always being there to talk to our members person to person. We believe the job of an insurance company is to pay out. That is what insurance is for. Most of our members have real life policies - policies that bring peace of mind during life, and genuine support in the event of death. We are not here to chase the super-rich with annuities and wealth management products. AAA has been one of the most trusted names in America because it believes in providing the services that middle class Americans need.

Responsibilities

The Role

You will join a small, newly formed, and highly visible Transformation Office responsible for leading the company’s most strategic, enterprise‑wide transformation initiatives. These programs are complex, mission‑critical, and backed by multi‑million‑dollar investments. As a key driver within the Transformation Office, you will translate strategy into execution—turning transformational vision into measurable outcomes and sustained business impact.

This is a high visibility Project Change Management Analyst role – serves as a central point of accountability for portfolio‑level performance, financial transparency, and delivery insight across IT initiatives. It partners closely with initiative leads, Finance, and Centers of Excellence to consolidate financial and delivery data into consistent, executive‑ready reporting, Steering Committees, and governance forums. The role ensures disciplined portfolio reporting across agile, waterfall, and hybrid efforts, proactively surfacing risks, dependencies, and performance gaps to enable informed decisions, strengthen governance, and drive value realization throughout the transformation.

The Next Phase

Our mission is to provide those services for as many people as we can. To achieve that we need to evolve. We need to boldly embrace innovation and technology. Your leadership will help us deliver on our mission together and achieve our transformation. At AAA Life, empathy and progress go hand in hand, creating a culture where bright ideas flourish and meaningful impact grows. If you are drawn to an environment that values purpose as much as potential, we invite you to join us. Because here, being there for people isn’t just a promise—it is our driving force.

Position Responsibilities

  • Track and report on IT project performance, including actual vs spend, forecasted costs, delivery milestones, and KPI progress 
  • Monitor financial performance across IT initiatives, ensuring alignment with budgets, forecasts, and expected value realization 
  • Consolidate updates from Transformation Office, Initiative Leads (including Product Owners and Scrum Masters), Finance and COE Managers into executive-ready reporting 
  • Identify, analyze, and escalate delivery risks, dependencies, and performance gaps 
  • Prepare standardized metrics reports and dashboards for Steering Committee (SteerCo), Technology Leadership, and executive stakeholders to support governance and decision‑making.
  • Partner with Finance to validate financial data, including capital vs. expense spend, labor, and vendor costs 
  • Ensure consistency and integrity of reporting across the IT portfolio, including adherence to PMO standards and governance frameworks 
  • Support reporting across Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid delivery methodologies 
  • Participate in recurring forums (e.g., IT Transformation stand-ups, finance reviews) to surface insights and ensure alignment 

Core Competencies – How You Will Contribute

  • Analytical Thinking: Ability to interpret financial and delivery data, identify trends, and generate actionable insights 
  • Financial Acumen: Understanding of IT budgeting, forecasting, and cost tracking (including Capital vs. Expense and Operating Expense) 
  • Data Visualization & Reporting: Ability to create clear, concise, and executive-ready reports and dashboards 
  • Attention to Detail: High level of accuracy in reporting, data validation, and reconciliation 
  • Communication Skills: Ability to translate technical and financial information into clear insights for non-technical stakeholders 
  • Stakeholder Management: Effective collaboration with IT, Finance, PMO, and business leaders 
  • Risk Awareness: Proactive identification and escalation of risks and issues 
  • Adaptability: Ability to operate in fast-paced, evolving IT and transformation environments 

Qualifications

Required Education/Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Business, Finance, Accounting, or a related field
  • 3–5 years of experience in IT project reporting, PMO, financial analysis, or technology program support
  • 2-5 years of experience supporting IT projects or transformation initiatives in Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid environments
  • 3-5 years of proficiency in Microsoft Office
  • 3-5 years of experience with project and portfolio management tools (e.g., Jira, Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, Clarity) preferred
  • 3-5 years of experience tracking IT financials, including resource costs, vendor spend, and infrastructure investments

Preferred Experience

  • Experience using Power BI and SQL analytics to track adoption, workforce readiness, and transformation KPIs, translating insights into executive‑ready reporting.
  • Proficiency with Atlassian Jira and Confluence to support agile delivery, transformation governance, and change documentation.
  • Experience with Monday.com or similar work‑management tools to coordinate cross‑functional initiatives and track transformation milestones.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) for leadership communications, dashboards, and reporting.

How You’ll Work

  • Work Solution: Hybrid (Tuesday- Thursday) or Remote (USA)
  • Relocation Eligibility: Available 

What We Bring to the Table

  • Hybrid work environment that promotes work-life balance
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage starting from your first day
  • Employer 401k match and employer contribution to a pension plan
  • Generous PTO and paid parental leave to support your family needs
  • Various associate resource groups and community involvement initiatives

Essential Job Functions 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle, or feel and talk or hear.  Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. 

 

This job requires the ability to perform duties contained in the job description for this position, including, but not limited to, the above requirements.  Reasonable accommodation will be provided for otherwise qualified applicants as needed to enable them to fulfill these requirements. 

 

AAA Life Insurance Company does not offer immigration sponsorship for this position. This includes visa types such as H-1B, TN, and STEM OPT. Please do not apply if you currently require or may require employer-sponsored immigration support now or in the future.

raw.description:
Meet the Moment with Alteryx

We're living through a once-in-a-generation shift in how work gets done. Data, automation, and AI are quickly becoming the center of every business decision - and Alteryx is leading the transformation.

You'll be working on the challenges that sit at the heart of modern business. No matter your role, the work you do will help organizations move faster, see more clearly, and tackle questions that used to feel impossible.

If you're ready to meet the moment with innovation, curiosity, and excellence, there's a place for you here.

About the Role

Alteryx is seeking a Senior Financial Analyst to join our Corporate Finance team. This highly visible role will support financial planning, forecasting, executive decision-making, and communications with the Board of Directors and investors.

You will play a key role in maintaining and enhancing the company’s long-term financial model, driving the monthly forecast process, and translating complex financial and operational data into clear, actionable insights. This is an ideal opportunity for a finance professional who combines strong financial modeling skills with advanced data-analysis capabilities and enjoys working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

What You’ll Do

  • Maintain, update, and improve the long-term financial model, including key operating assumptions, financial statements, cash flow, and scenario analyses.

  • Lead the annual operating plan (AOP) process, coordinating planning activities across the organization, challenging assumptions, developing executive recommendations, and delivering a comprehensive financial plan that supports Alteryx's strategic priorities.

  • Help lead the monthly forecasting process in partnership with functional FP&A teams, Accounting, and business leaders.

  • Prepare monthly and quarterly variance analyses against plan, forecast, and prior-period results. Analyze financial performance, key business drivers, trends, risks, and opportunities.

  • Support the development of Board of Directors, investor, and executive leadership materials.

  • Build clear, compelling financial analyses and presentations that support strategic decision-making.

  • Partner with business-unit FP&A teams, Accounting, Finance Systems, and other cross-functional teams to ensure financial information is accurate, consistent, and timely.

  • Develop dashboards, reporting tools, and recurring analyses that improve visibility into business performance.

  • Use data and technology to automate manual processes, improve forecasting accuracy, and enhance the scalability of Corporate Finance workflows.

  • Support strategic projects and ad hoc analyses across the organization.

What We’re Looking For

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, Data Analytics, or a related field.

  • Relevant experience in financial planning and analysis, corporate finance, investment banking, management consulting, public accounting, or a similar analytical role.

  • Strong financial modeling skills, including experience with long-range planning, forecasting, and integrated financial statements.

  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience working with large, complex datasets.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with exceptional attention to detail.

  • Ability to communicate complex financial information clearly and concisely to executive audiences.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced environment.

  • Strong collaboration skills and the ability to build effective relationships across functions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Anaplan or another enterprise planning platform.

  • Familiarity with SQL, Alteryx, business intelligence tools, or data-visualization applications.

  • Experience preparing materials for executive leadership, Boards of Directors, or investors.

  • Experience in software, technology, or a recurring-revenue business.

  • Familiarity with SaaS financial and operating metrics.

  • MBA, CPA, CFA, or another relevant advanced degree or professional designation.

Why Join Alteryx

This role offers the opportunity to work closely with senior leaders, influence strategic and financial decisions, and help shape the processes and insights that support Alteryx’s long-term growth. You will join a collaborative Corporate Finance team and have the opportunity to use both finance and technology to improve how the company plans, analyzes, and communicates performance.

Compensation

Alteryx is committed to fair, equitable, and transparent compensation. Final compensation is determined by several factors, including but not limited to relevant work experience, education, certifications, skills, and geographic location.

The base salary range for this role in the United States is $103,000 - $135,000. This role is also eligible for a target annual bonus of 15% of base salary, based on individual and company performance.

In addition to base pay and bonus eligibility, this role includes clear forms of additional compensation, such as:

  • A monthly Connectivity Plus stipend of $150 to support remote work-related expenses

  • An annual $200 home office reimbursement

Alteryx offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial security, and overall well-being, including:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • 401(k) with company match

  • Paid parental leave, caregiver leave, and flexible time off

  • Mental health support and wellness reimbursement

  • Career development and education assistance

Find yourself checking a lot of these boxes but doubting whether you should apply? At Alteryx, we support a growth mindset for our associates through all stages of their careers. If you meet some of the requirements and you share our values, we encourage you to apply. As part of our ongoing commitment to a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace, we’re invested in building teams with a wide variety of backgrounds, identities, and experiences.

Benefits & Perks:

Alteryx has amazing benefits for all Associates which can be viewed here.

For roles in San Francisco and Los Angeles: Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Alteryx will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

This position involves access to software/technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant’s capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls.
